name: platform-http
title: Platform HTTP
description: Expose HTTP endpoints using the HTTP server available in the current platform.
label: http

properties.name: path
properties.description: The path under which this endpoint serves the HTTP requests, for proxy use 'proxy'

properties.name: consumes
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: The content type this endpoint accepts as an input, such as application/xml or application/json. null or */* mean no restriction.

properties.name: cookieDomain
properties.description: Sets which server can receive cookies.

properties.name: cookieHttpOnly
properties.description: Sets whether to prevent client side scripts from accessing created cookies.

properties.name: cookieMaxAge
properties.description: Sets the maximum cookie age in seconds.

properties.name: cookiePath
properties.description: Sets the URL path that must exist in the requested URL in order to send the Cookie.

properties.name: cookieSameSite
properties.description: Sets whether to prevent the browser from sending cookies along with cross-site requests.

properties.name: cookieSecure
properties.description: Sets whether the cookie is only sent to the server with an encrypted request over HTTPS.

properties.name: handleWriteResponseError
properties.label: advanced,consumer
properties.description: When Camel is complete processing the message, and the HTTP server is writing response. This option controls whether Camel should catch any failure during writing response and store this on the Exchange, which allows onCompletion/UnitOfWork to regard the Exchange as failed and have access to the caused exception from the HTTP server.

properties.name: httpMethodRestrict
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: A comma separated list of HTTP methods to serve, e.g. GET,POST . If no methods are specified, all methods will be served.

properties.name: matchOnUriPrefix
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Whether or not the consumer should try to find a target consumer by matching the URI prefix if no exact match is found.

properties.name: muteException
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: If enabled and an Exchange failed processing on the consumer side the response's body won't contain the exception's stack trace.

properties.name: populateBodyWithForm
properties.label: advanced,consumer
properties.description: Whether to populate the message Body with a Map containing application/x-www-form-urlencoded form properties.

properties.name: produces
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: The content type this endpoint produces, such as application/xml or application/json.

properties.name: requestTimeout
properties.label: advanced,consumer
properties.description: The period in milliseconds after which the request should be timed out.

properties.name: returnHttpRequestHeaders
properties.label: advanced,consumer
properties.description: Whether to include HTTP request headers (Accept, User-Agent, etc.) into HTTP response produced by this endpoint.

properties.name: useBodyHandler
properties.label: advanced,consumer
properties.description: Whether to use BodyHandler for the request. If set to false then the request will no be read and parsed.

properties.name: useCookieHandler
properties.label: advanced,consumer
properties.description: Whether to enable the Cookie Handler that allows Cookie addition, expiry, and retrieval (currently only supported by camel-platform-http-vertx)

properties.name: useStreaming
properties.label: advanced,consumer
properties.description: Whether to use streaming for large requests and responses (currently only supported by camel-platform-http-vertx)

properties.name: bridgeErrorHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exceptionHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exchangePattern
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

properties.name: fileNameExtWhitelist
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: A comma or whitespace separated list of file extensions. Uploads having these extensions will be stored locally. Null value or asterisk () will allow all files.

properties.name: headerFilterStrategy
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: To use a custom HeaderFilterStrategy to filter headers to and from Camel message.

properties.name: platformHttpEngine
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: An HTTP Server engine implementation to serve the requests of this endpoint.

properties.name: oauthProfile
properties.label: consumer,security
properties.description: OAuth profile name for validating incoming Authorization: Bearer tokens. When set, the request is authenticated before the route is processed. This requires an OAuthTokenValidationFactory; camel-oauth provides the default implementation.
